business_problem: AT&T needed to retire costly on-premises data lake infrastructure because silos, schema sprawl, and heavy operational burden were slowing data democratization and AI adoption across the enterprise.
solution_summary: AT&T uses Azure Databricks and Power BI to support Azure Databricks data platform migration. AT&T needed to retire costly on-premises data lake infrastructure because silos, schema sprawl, and heavy operational burden were slowing data democratization and AI adoption across the enterprise. In practice, the implementation runs transformation or AI logic on Azure Databricks, and delivers outputs through Power BI. Legacy operational and analytics data are consolidated into a governed cloud data layer; Azure Databricks applies analytics or model logic; results are surfaced through Power BI. The case study reports Celebrating datacenter yields of 300% ROI, showing measurable improvement after the rollout.
business_outcome: AT&T reported Celebrating datacenter yields of 300% ROI, improving Azure Databricks data platform migration with measurable gains in cost reduction, productivity improvement, scalability, and speed to market.
evidence_quotes: AT&T migration to Azure Databricks catalyzes technical staff, advances business goals
AT&T’s on-premises data architecture prevented decision-makers from connecting to a single source of truth and created data silos, costly compute workarounds, and barriers to innovation.
Deploying a thoughtful, strategic approach to massive data migration
Transforming company data culture with modern cloud architecture
